The romance genre is often stereotyped as having writing on par with 50 Shades Of Grey, a plot that makes The Rocky Horror Picture Show look coherent, the same level of characterization as Tetris, and having numerous other damning traits. I've heard of people taking turns reading (specifically Harlequin) romance novels aloud, with the rest of the group making rocky horror style callbacks at them because they were that awful.

While I personally am unfamiliar with the genre, I don't think that an entire genre could truly be as bad as romance is stereotyped to be, and I would be interested in hearing what those more familiar with the genre have to say.
Are there any real gems of the romance genre, or is it truly as bad as the stereotypes?

I read a fair bit of romance (and even writing that feels a bit shameful!). There is a lot of crap but there's also a lot that is well written, fast paced and character driven. I love books in series and that's really common in romance. Sometimes you don't want to be challenged when you read, you just want to spend time being comfortable and having fun - that's what romance books are for.

A bit like porn, there is something for everyone. Want straight up sex? Read A Gentleman in the Street by Alisha Rai. Want crime /detective fiction? Read the Phryne Fisher or In Death series. There's sure to be a poorly written dolphin/mermaid/alien book out there if that's your thing.
